subject: Computer Networking
title: Infrastructure as Code
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Infrastructure as Code.

hook.text: Define your network in a text file. Infrastructure as Code makes it reproducible and versioned.

buildup.text: Terraform and Ansible define configs declaratively. Describe the desired state; the tool enforces it.

discovery.text: Changes go through code review and version control. Every change has an author and a rollback path.

twist.text: IaC kills config drift. The code is truth. If a device deviates, the tool detects and corrects it.

climax.text: Netflix deploys thousands of network changes weekly with IaC. Manual config at that scale? Impossible.

punchline.text: Infrastructure as Code: version-controlled, reviewable, repeatable.

quiz.question: What problem does Infrastructure as Code solve?
options: Manual configuration drift and unreproducible network setups
The cost of buying network hardware

details.summary: Infrastructure as code manages network devices through version-controlled configuration files rather than manual CLI commands.
details.whyItMatters: Manual network configuration is slow, error-prone, and impossible to scale. Infrastructure as code brings the rigor of software development to network operations, making changes repeatable and auditable.
takeaways: Network configuration is defined in version-controlled code files
Automated deployment ensures consistent configuration at scale
Version control enables easy rollback of problematic changes

faq.question: What tools are used for network infrastructure as code?
faq.answer: Ansible is popular for network device configuration with agentless SSH-based operation. Terraform manages cloud network resources declaratively. Nornir is a Python framework for network automation. NAPALM provides a vendor-neutral interface for network device management.

faq.question: How does IaC improve network reliability?
faq.answer: IaC eliminates manual typing errors that cause outages. Changes are reviewed in code review before deployment. Automated testing validates configurations before pushing to production. Version control tracks every change with who made it and why. Rollback is instant if a change causes problems.
